name: Illuminated Sign
author: Jonesie

parts.label: End cap (same colour as the box)

notes: A light-box sign: a black, light-tight box with one clear front panel that slides in from the right — no screws, glue or hardware to change the text. The right-hand end of the panel is a flush end cap, in the same colour as the box, that completes the box end, so when it is in nothing sticks out; to change the lettering or reach the lights, work a fingernail or a thin blade into the seam at the end and slide the panel out. How it works: print the panel in clear (transparent) filament, then paint the front face black or a very dark colour, to match the box. The black blocks the light; the engraved letters are recesses, so they stay clear and glow. Print the box on its back with the open front facing up, no supports; print the panel and its end cap flat, text side up, no supports. The cap is a separate part so it prints in the box colour; a tongue on the panel locks into a pocket in the cap, so on a multi-colour printer they print together as one piece, and on a single-colour printer print them separately and glue the tongue into the cap. Box: black, with at least 4 walls (or 100% infill) — it must be dense enough that no light shines through the walls, and PLA or PETG both work. Panel: clear PETG, 100% infill, 0.2 mm layers, printed slowly; it comes out frosted rather than glass-clear, which spreads the light nicely. Painting: lightly scuff the front face, then roll or dab on matte black acrylic (or whatever dark colour matches your box) with a small foam roller or foam brush, which only touches the raised surface and leaves the engraved letters clear. Two thin coats block the light better than one thick one. If paint gets into a letter, wipe it out with a cotton bud while it is wet. Spray paint works too if you mask the letters or wipe them clean afterwards. For lights, stick a USB or 5 V LED strip (warm white, or colour) around the inside of the box, and feed the cable out through the 8 mm power hole in the back wall (bottom right) — wide enough for a USB-C or barrel-jack lead with its plug. Use LEDs only — a candle or tea light will soften the print. Small heat vents run through the top wall and both side walls; they are narrow slits, but if any light shows through, cover them on the inside with a dab of black paint or tape. To hang or fix the sign, four countersunk 3.6 mm holes go through the back panel; with the front panel slid out you can reach the screw heads from inside, so screw straight into the wall or a board. The panel is held by a close sliding fit (about 0.2 mm of clearance), so if it works loose a dab of removable putty at the end holds it; that gap also lets a little light seep at the edges, which black tape over the slot cures.
